mainTopic: Carrying among roofs, courtyards, and enclosures on שבת: the views of רבי מאיר, חכמים, and רבי שמעון, the supporting ברייתות, and whether the הלכה follows רבי שמעון with or without an עירוב
overview: This amud finishes רב יהודה's summary of the משנה's three opinions. For רבי מאיר, roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are each separate domains. For חכמים, roofs and courtyards are one domain and enclosures are another. For רבי שמעון, all of them are one domain. The גמרא brings a ברייתא supporting רב's reading that חכמים allow only four אמות on each roof. It then brings רבי's story about רבי שמעון in תקוע, which supports רב יהודה. A second story, from רבי יהודה, about carrying a ספר תורה during persecution is rejected, because a time of danger proves nothing. On the הלכה, רב follows רבי שמעון only when no עירוב was made, because of a protective decree. שמואל and רבי יוחנן follow רבי שמעון in every case. רב חסדא's challenge to them is answered: רבי שמעון does not make such decrees, as his three-courtyard case shows. Finally, רב ששת challenges רב from the wording of the משנה and answers himself: a hat or shawl worn into the courtyard is a house vessel found there even without an עירוב.

steps.title: End of רב יהודה's three-way breakdown of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רב יהודה's summary. For רבי מאיר, enclosures are their own domain. For חכמים, roofs and courtyards form one domain and enclosures form another. For רבי שמעון, everything is one domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: …enclosures are a domain of their own. According to חכמים, roofs and courtyards are one domain, and enclosures are one domain. According to רבי שמעון, all of them are one domain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement by רב יהודה that lays out how each of the three opinions in the משנה divides roofs, courtyards, and enclosures into domains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is the strictest: each type of area is its own domain, so you may carry within a type but not from one type to another. חכמים join roofs and courtyards into one domain but keep enclosures separate. רבי שמעון is the most lenient and treats all three as one big domain for objects that were in them when שבת began.

keyTerms.meaning: Enclosures: fenced-in open areas, usually outside the houses, not used for living
A domain of their own, which you cannot carry into from other types of areas
Roofs
Courtyards
One domain, so carrying among its parts is allowed

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of רב יהודה's statement. The first line, 'enclosures are a domain of their own,' is the last part of רבי מאיר's opinion as רב יהודה explains it. It is not a new opinion.

phrases.english: Enclosures are a domain of their own.
phrases.notes: This is the last part of רבי מאיר's view, the way רב יהודה tells it.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים: גַּגִּין וַחֲצֵירוֹת רְשׁוּת אַחַת,
phrases.english: According to the Sages: roofs and courtyards are one domain,
enclosures are one domain.
phrases.notes: Enclosures are a separate domain from the roofs and courtyards.

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: כּוּלָּן רְשׁוּת אַחַת הֵן.
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon: all of them are one domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵי חֲכָמִים: גַּגִּין וַחֲצֵירוֹת רְשׁוּת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's statement, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are each a separate domain. חכמים: roofs and courtyards are one domain, and enclosures are another. רבי שמעון: all are one domain.

steps.title: Announcing support for both רב and רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is one ברייתא that backs רב and another that backs רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רב, and a ברייתא was taught in line with רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is announcing that it will now quote two ברייתות, one backing רב and one backing רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read חכמים as saying each roof is its own domain, with only four אמות of carrying. רב יהודה read חכמים as joining roofs and courtyards into one domain. The גמרא shows that each of them has a ברייתא supporting a different part of his position.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים not included in the משנה)
In line with him; supporting his view

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav,
a baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב, תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from presenting the opinions to bringing proof for them.
steps.raayaObject: The readings of רב and of רב יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות, quoted in the next steps.

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רב: under חכמים each roof is its own domain
steps.stepSummary: In this ברייתא, רבי מאיר says all the roofs of a city are one domain but forbids carrying between roofs and courtyards. חכמים say each roof is its own domain, where one may carry only four אמות. This matches רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the roofs of the city are one domain. It is forbidden to carry things up or down from the roofs to the courtyard or from the courtyard to the roofs. Things that were in the courtyard when שבת began may be carried in the courtyard. Things that were on the roofs may be carried on the roofs, as long as one roof is not ten טפחים higher or lower than the next. This is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say each and every one is its own domain, and one may carry on it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first ברייתא. Its version of חכמים says each roof is its own separate domain with only four אמות of carrying, which is exactly how רב understood them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said חכמים treat roofs and courtyards as one domain. This ברייתא instead has חכמים saying 'each one is its own domain' with only four אמות, which supports רב. In this ברייתא, רבי מאיר never allows carrying between roofs and courtyards. He does allow carrying from roof to roof, but only if no roof is ten טפחים higher or lower than its neighbor.

keyTerms.meaning: To carry up and to carry down (between roof and courtyard)
That 'rested' there, meaning they were in that place when שבת began
To move or carry them
Ten טפחים higher, a height difference that separates the roofs into different areas
Within four אמות, the minimal space where carrying is always allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's strict reading of חכמים has a source from the תנאים. That makes it a strong position in the debate over what חכמים hold.

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל גַּגּוֹת הָעִיר רְשׁוּת אַחַת הֵן,
phrases.english: All the roofs of the city are one domain,
and it is forbidden to carry up or carry down

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַגַּגִּין לֶחָצֵר וּמִן הֶחָצֵר לְגַגִּין.
phrases.english: from the roofs to the courtyard or from the courtyard to the roofs.
And vessels that were in the courtyard when Shabbat began —
it is permitted to carry them in the courtyard;
those on the roofs — it is permitted to carry them on the roofs,
provided that a roof is not
ten handbreadths higher or ten handbreadths lower,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
each and every one is a domain of its own,
and one may carry on it only within four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two promised ברייתות.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that, according to חכמים, one may carry only four אמות on each roof.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which חכמים say 'each one is its own domain, only four אמות.'

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רב יהודה: רבי's story about רבי שמעון in תקוע
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells how, while learning with רבי שמעון in תקוע, they carried oil and a towel through roofs, courtyards, and enclosures to reach the spring. This supports רב יהודה's reading of רבי שמעון that all of these areas are one domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: When we were learning Torah with רבי שמעון in תקוע, we would carry oil and a towel from roof to roof, from roof to courtyard, from courtyard to courtyard, from courtyard to enclosure, and from enclosure to another enclosure, until we reached the spring where we bathed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second ברייתא, a real-life story. It shows that רבי שמעון's students carried freely across roofs, courtyards, and enclosures, just as רב יהודה said רבי שמעון allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said that, according to רבי שמעון, roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are all one domain. Here, under רבי שמעון's guidance, the students carried through every combination, including into enclosures. That is practical proof of רב יהודה's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: תקוע, the town where רבי שמעון taught
A bath towel
We would carry (literally, 'bring up')
A spring

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
Rebbi said: When we were studying Torah
with Rabbi Shimon in Tekoa,
we would carry oil and a towel
from roof to roof, and from roof to courtyard,
and from courtyard to courtyard, and from courtyard to enclosure,
and from enclosure to another enclosure,
until we reached the spring
in which we would bathe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second promised ברייתא, this time supporting רב יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading that, according to רבי שמעון, roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are all one domain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's eyewitness account of what was done in רבי שמעון's presence.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story of carrying a ספר תורה in a time of danger
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reports that during a time of persecution they carried a ספר תורה from courtyard to roof, roof to courtyard, and courtyard to enclosure in order to read from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was an incident during a time of danger, and we would carry a ספר תורה from courtyard to roof, from roof to courtyard, and from courtyard to enclosure, to read from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second report, this one from רבי יהודה. During a time of persecution, they carried a ספר תורה between courtyards, roofs, and enclosures so they could read from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another real-life case of carrying across all three types of areas, including into an enclosure. It fits the broad, lenient approach that רב יהודה attributes to רבי שמעון. The 'time of danger' explains why they had to move the ספר תורה secretly from place to place.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a real-life case
A time of danger, when the government banned Torah observance
To read from it

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of חכמים. רב: each roof is its own domain, with only four אמות. רב יהודה: roofs and courtyards are one domain. A ברייתא backs רב on חכמים, and the stories from רבי שמעון's circle back רב יהודה's reading that, for רבי שמעון, roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are all one domain.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident in a time of danger,
and we would carry a Torah scroll
from courtyard to roof, and from roof to courtyard,
and from courtyard to enclosure, to read from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second report alongside רבי's story, describing similar carrying across all three types of areas.
steps.raayaObject: That carrying among courtyards, roofs, and enclosures was actually practiced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's report of an incident during a time of persecution.

steps.title: A time of danger proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה: what people did during persecution cannot teach us the normal הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A time of danger is no proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יהודה's story about carrying the ספר תורה during the persecution. They say it does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a time of danger, people may do things that are normally forbidden only מדרבנן. So the fact that they carried the ספר תורה between courtyard, roof and enclosure does not show that this is allowed on an ordinary שבת. Only רבי יהודה's proof is knocked down. רבי's story about רבי שמעון in תקוע was not a danger case, so it is not affected.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the חכמים) said to him
A time of danger or persecution
Proof

steps.confusionAlert: This rejection is aimed only at רבי יהודה's persecution story from Step 5. It is not aimed at רבי's story about רבי שמעון from Step 4.

phrases.english: They said to him:
A time of danger is no proof.
phrases.notes: In danger, rabbinic prohibitions may be set aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין שְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה רְאָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the persecution story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A danger situation is an exception and cannot teach the normal law

steps.title: Quoting רבי שמעון's view in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words of רבי שמעון to begin a new discussion about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Roofs, courtyards and enclosures are all one domain, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the start of רבי שמעון's statement in the משנה. This sets up the next move, which is a discussion of whether the הלכה follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that roofs, courtyards and enclosures are one domain for objects that were already in those areas when שבת began. Objects that started שבת inside the houses are not included. The וכו׳ means the rest of the משנה's wording is understood.

keyTerms.meaning: Roofs
All are one (domain)
Etc.; the quote continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Roofs, etc., are all one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֶחָד גַּגִּין וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the proofs to a new heading from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roofs, courtyards and enclosures form one domain for objects that began שבת there

steps.title: רב rules like רבי שמעון only without an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי שמעון only when the courtyards did not make an עירוב, out of concern that house objects might be carried too far.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון, provided they did not make an עירוב. But if they made an עירוב, no, because we decree that perhaps a person will come to take out vessels from the houses to the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the practical הלכה. It follows רבי שמעון, but only when each courtyard did not make its own עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a courtyard has an עירוב, people may bring objects from their houses into that courtyard. Those objects would then be mixed with the courtyard objects. Someone might then carry the house objects on to a roof or another courtyard, which even רבי שמעון forbids. Without an עירוב, house objects never reach the courtyard, so there is no mix-up and רבי שמעון's leniency stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They made an עירוב (joined the courtyard's houses)
We make a rabbinic decree
Perhaps he will come (to do something forbidden)
Vessels or objects from the houses

steps.confusionAlert: It looks backwards, but making an עירוב here leads to a stricter result. The עירוב lets house objects into the courtyard, and that creates the risk the decree is guarding against.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical limit on רבי שמעון's leniency, and שמואל and רבי יוחנן will dispute it.

phrases.english: Rav said: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
provided that they did not make an eiruv.
But if they made an eiruv, no,
because we decree lest one come
to take out house vessels to the courtyard.
phrases.notes: He might then carry them on to another domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְהוּא שֶׁלֹּא עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the view of רבי שמעון quoted in Step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון only when no separate עירוב was made, because of a rabbinic decree

steps.title: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון in every case
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules like רבי שמעון whether or not the courtyards made an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Whether they made an עירוב or did not make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not accept רב's decree. In his view, people will not confuse house objects with courtyard objects. So רבי שמעון's leniency applies whether or not there was an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who often disputes רב
Whether ... or ...

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
Whether they made an eiruv or did not make an eiruv.
phrases.notes: The halakha follows רבי שמעון either way.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: בֵּין עֵירְבוּ בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא עֵירְבוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's limit from Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון with or without an עירוב

steps.title: רבי יוחנן sides with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees with שמואל and sharply asks who invented the difference between having an עירוב and not having one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly רבי יוחנן said: Who whispered to you that there is a difference whether they made an עירוב or did not make an עירוב?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן backs up שמואל's view. He mocks the idea that an עירוב should make any difference here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "who whispered to you" means that no real source supports the distinction. This rejects רב's decree and adds a second great authority to שמואל's side. So רבי שמעון's leniency holds in all cases.

keyTerms.meaning: And similarly said (agreeing)
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל
Who whispered to you? (There is no source for this)

steps.whatToRemember: רב limits the ruling like רבי שמעון to courtyards without an עירוב, because of a decree about house objects. שמואל and רבי יוחנן rule like רבי שמעון whether or not there was an עירוב.

phrases.english: And similarly Rabbi Yochanan said:
Who whispered to you,
phrases.notes: Meaning: who told you this? There is no basis for it.

phrases.english: whether they made an eiruv or did not make an eiruv?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מִי לְחָשְׁךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports שמואל from Step 9 against רב from Step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No distinction is made based on an עירוב; the הלכה follows רבי שמעון

steps.title: רב חסדא: two vessels in one courtyard, one allowed and one forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא challenges שמואל and רבי יוחנן. If the courtyards made an עירוב, people will see two vessels in the same courtyard with different rules, which is confusing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא strongly objects: according to שמואל and רבי יוחנן, people will say, 'Here are two vessels in one courtyard, and this one is allowed while that one is forbidden!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the view of שמואל and רבי יוחנן, who said we follow רבי שמעון even when the courtyards made an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When there is an עירוב, people may carry house vessels out into the courtyard. Now a vessel that started שבת in the courtyard may be moved to another courtyard, but a vessel that started שבת in the house may not. Both vessels are lying in the same courtyard, so people will mix them up. That is exactly the worry רב raised.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (a sharp challenge, usually based on logic)
Vessels or utensils
Permitted / forbidden
People will say (they will draw a mistaken conclusion)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda strongly objects to it:
According to Shmuel and Rabbi Yochanan, people will say:
Two vessels in one courtyard,
phrases.notes: One vessel started שבת in the courtyard, and the other was brought out from the house.

phrases.english: This one is permitted and that one is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the position just stated by שמואל and רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל and רבי יוחנן's ruling that we follow רבי שמעון even with an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With an עירוב, vessels with different rules end up side by side in one courtyard. That invites confusion, so we should forbid it, as רב said.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not make protective decrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון stays consistent with his usual approach: he does not issue decrees out of fear of confusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning, because he does not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב חסדא's challenge. This line states the answer briefly, and the next steps will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's worry is a reason to make a גזירה, a protective rule. The answer is that רבי שמעון, as a general matter, does not make that kind of גזירה. So the fear of confusion does not change his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his view elsewhere)
He made a decree (a protective rabbinic prohibition)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
That he does not make a decree.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Consistency with the author's known approach: he does not make decrees.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We should worry about confusion between the two vessels and forbid both.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון does not decree because of such confusion.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's case of three courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in which רבי שמעון describes three courtyards in a row. The middle one may carry with each outer one, but the two outer ones may not carry with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: רבי שמעון said, 'What is this like? It is like three courtyards that open into each other and also open into the public domain. If the two outer ones each made an עירוב with the middle one, the middle one is permitted with them and they are permitted with it, but the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a source to prove that רבי שמעון does not make decrees out of fear of confusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each outer courtyard joined in an עירוב with the middle one, but the two outer courtyards did not join with each other. As a result, vessels from both outer courtyards can end up in the middle courtyard, even though they may not be carried from one outer courtyard to the other. The next step explains how this proves our point.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (introduces a quote from a משנה)
To what is this matter comparable?
The outer ones (the two end courtyards)
The middle one
The public domain

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Shimon said:
To what is this matter comparable?
To three courtyards that open into each other
And also open into the public domain,
And the two outer ones made an eiruv with the middle one —

phrases.aramaic: הִיא מוּתֶּרֶת עִמָּהֶן, וְהֵן מוּתָּרוֹת עִמָּהּ,
phrases.english: It is permitted with them, and they are permitted with it,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁתֵּי הַחִיצוֹנוֹת אֲסוּרִין זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
phrases.english: But the two outer ones are forbidden with each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports the answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not decree out of fear that vessels with different rules will be mixed up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of three courtyards in רבי שמעון's name.

steps.title: Applying the three-courtyard case to house vessels
steps.stepSummary: In the three-courtyard case, רבי שמעון did not worry that vessels from one outer courtyard would be carried to the other. In the same way, he does not worry that house vessels will be carried to another courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: There he did not decree out of fear that someone might carry vessels from this courtyard to that courtyard. So too here, we do not decree out of fear that someone might take house vessels out to the courtyard (and then on to another courtyard).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by showing how the three-courtyard case matches our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the middle courtyard, vessels from both outer courtyards lie side by side. Still, רבי שמעון did not forbid carrying for fear that someone would take a vessel from one outer courtyard into the other. The same logic applies when house vessels and courtyard vessels lie together, so רב חסדא's objection is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps he will come to (do something wrong)
To take out
Vessels or utensils (Aramaic for כֵּלִים)
So too (here)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון does not make a גזירה just because vessels with different rules lie next to each other. This defends שמואל and רבי יוחנן, who apply his leniency even when there is an עירוב.

phrases.english: And he did not decree, out of fear that one might come

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מָאנֵי דְּהָא חָצֵר לְהָא חָצֵר,
phrases.english: To take out vessels of this courtyard to that courtyard,
phrases.notes: That is, from one outer courtyard to the other outer courtyard.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי לָא גָּזְרִינַן דִּילְמָא אָתֵי
phrases.english: So too we do not decree, out of fear that one might come
To take out house vessels to the courtyard.
phrases.notes: The worry is that he would then carry them on from there to another courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source from step 13 to finish answering step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to a parallel case where רבי שמעון also did not decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mixed vessels in one courtyard should cause a prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: Just as he did not decree in the three-courtyard case, he does not decree here either.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes רבי שמעון on vessels from the house
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת begins an objection by quoting רבי שמעון: roofs, courtyards, and enclosures count as one domain for vessels that started שבת in them, but not for vessels that started שבת in the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת raised an objection: רבי שמעון says, 'Roofs, courtyards, and enclosures are all one domain for vessels that rested in them when שבת began, but not for vessels that rested inside the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a challenge. Here he only quotes the source text, and the next step will show how he uses it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון specifically excludes 'vessels that were in the house.' He is talking about house vessels that are now outside in the courtyard. רב ששת will ask how such vessels got into the courtyard in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection from a source
Roofs
Enclosures (fenced areas, usually behind houses)
That 'rested,' meaning they were located there when שבת began
One domain

phrases.aramaic: מֵתִיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection: Rabbi Shimon says,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גַּגּוֹת אֶחָד חֲצֵירוֹת וְאֶחָד קַרְפֵּיפוֹת
phrases.english: Roofs, courtyards, and enclosures alike
Are one domain
For vessels that were inside them when Shabbat began,
But not for vessels that were inside the house when Shabbat began.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, this time aimed at רב's position from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that רבי שמעון's leniency applies only when the courtyards did not make an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source text itself mentions house vessels sitting in the courtyard. This suggests that רבי שמעון is discussing a case with an עירוב.

steps.title: House vessels in the courtyard point to an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת argues that if the courtyards made an עירוב, it makes sense that house vessels could be found in the courtyard. So רבי שמעון's words fit a case with an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well if you say they made an עירוב: that is how you can find house vessels in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the first half of his argument. He shows that the משנה fits a case with an עירוב, and the other half of his question continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, nobody may carry from a house into a shared courtyard, so house vessels should never be there at all. With an עירוב, people may carry them out, and that is why רבי שמעון needed to say they cannot go further. This points against רב, who limited רבי שמעון to cases without an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well if you say (the first half of a 'this works, but that doesn't' argument)
That is how you find it (how this case can happen)
They made an עירוב (joined their properties so carrying is allowed)

steps.confusionAlert: רב ששת is attacking רב here, not שמואל or רבי יוחנן. His argument supports the view that רבי שמעון was speaking about a case where there was an עירוב.

phrases.english: It works well if you say that they made an eiruv —
That is how you can find
House vessels in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב ששת's objection by explaining what the quoted source implies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's limitation of רבי שמעון to courtyards without an עירוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: House vessels can only reach the courtyard if there was an עירוב. Since רבי שמעון talks about such vessels, he must be discussing a case with an עירוב.

steps.title: Without an עירוב, how could house vessels reach the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת finishes his objection. If there was no עירוב, it seems impossible for house vessels to be in the courtyard, so רבי שמעון must be talking about a case with an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say רבי שמעון is talking about a case where they did not make an עירוב, how could you ever find house vessels in the courtyard?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת completes the objection he began in the last two steps. He shows that the case of 'house vessels in the courtyard' seems impossible without an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without an עירוב, you may not carry from a house into the courtyard. So house vessels should never be found there, and רבי שמעון's rule about them would be pointless. That suggests רבי שמעון was talking about a case with an עירוב, which goes against רב's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces the other possibility)
Where they did not make an עירוב
How can you find such a case?
House vessels: items that started שבת inside the house

steps.confusionAlert: This objection is not against רבי שמעון himself. It challenges the claim that רבי שמעון's rule applies when there was no עירוב, which is רב's position.

phrases.english: But if you say it is where they did not make an eruv —
phrases.notes: The other side of the either/or that began in step 16.

phrases.english: how can you find it,
phrases.notes: A common phrase asking whether a case could ever happen.

phrases.english: house vessels in the courtyard?
phrases.notes: Without an עירוב, nobody could carry them out there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ בְּשֶׁלֹּא עֵירְבוּ הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the either/or argument from step 16. With an עירוב the case works, but without one it seems impossible.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that רבי שמעון's rule applies where no עירוב was made.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without an עירוב, house vessels cannot legally reach the courtyard. So רבי שמעון's mention of house vessels in the courtyard must be about a case with an עירוב.

steps.title: רב ששת answers himself: a hat or a shawl
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת raised the objection and also answered it. A hat or shawl can be worn from the house into the courtyard, so house vessels can be there even without an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked the question and he answered it: the case is a hat or a shawl.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers his own objection. He shows a realistic way house vessels could be in the courtyard even without an עירוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person may wear a hat or shawl from the house into the courtyard, because wearing clothing is not carrying. Once he takes it off there, it is a house vessel sitting in the courtyard. רבי שמעון's rule now makes sense without an עירוב, so רב's position is defended.

keyTerms.term: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
keyTerms.meaning: He raised the objection and he answered it himself
A hat or cap
A shawl or scarf

steps.whatToRemember: The objection to רב is answered. Even without an עירוב, house vessels can reach the courtyard if they are worn there, like a hat or shawl. So רבי שמעון's rule fits רב's reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that wearing clothing from one area into another is not carrying. That is why a realistic case of house vessels in the courtyard exists even without an עירוב.

phrases.english: He raised the objection
and he resolved it:
phrases.notes: The same person who asked also answers.

phrases.english: with a hat or a shawl.
phrases.notes: Worn out of the house and then taken off in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מוֹתֵיב לַהּ וְהוּא מְפָרֵק לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the objection raised in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: finds a realistic situation that makes the rule work without an עירוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: House vessels could only reach the courtyard by carrying, which requires an עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Clothing worn from the house, like a hat or shawl, reaches the courtyard without carrying. So the case exists even without an עירוב, and רב's reading stands.
